more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Isopropyl citrate is a mixture of mono-, di- and triisopropyl esters of citric acid. These components are made by esterifying citric acid with isopropanol. FDA lists antioxidant, metal-binding and solvent functions for the preparation. The specified food applications include margarine, non-alcoholic beverages, fats and oils, subject to manufacturing conditions.
more_info.origin: Manufactured by esterifying citric acid with isopropanol. The resulting synthetic ester mixture contains mono-, di- and triisopropyl citrate. The regulation does not identify the feedstock route used to make every batch of citric acid.
more_info.uses: The US regulation lists margarine, non-alcoholic beverages, fats and oils. The preparation can serve antioxidant, metal-binding or solvent functions, with the amount limited by the stated manufacturing conditions.
